text: Denied by health insurance? Map the evidence, deadlines, internal appeal, and next review step.
A free fill-in insurance appeal letter, plus what to attach and how to prove you filed it.
“Not medically necessary”? Ask which clinical criterion was not met, then answer it with evidence.
Prior-auth denials can be administrative, clinical, or step-therapy related. Identify which one first.
“Try the cheaper drug first” may allow exceptions for prior failures, contraindications, or likely harm.
A formulary exception usually must address each covered alternative. Organize the evidence first.
Out-of-network denials can involve emergency care, network gaps, or billing. Identify the rule first.
Called “experimental”? Request the exact policy and evidence cutoff, then compare your record to it.
Internal appeal denied? An independent external review may be next. Check eligibility and deadlines.
ER denied as “not an emergency”? Coverage is judged by symptoms at the door, not the final diagnosis.
Therapy denied? Federal parity law limits how much stricter mental health rules can be than medical.
Denied in California? Free Independent Medical Review has overturned many denials — here's how to file.
GLP-1 denied? Check whether it is a plan exclusion or a criteria review — they need different appeals.
MRI or CT denied? The fastest route back is usually a peer-to-peer your doctor can request.
